title: Sell Mineral Rights in Broadus, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Broadus, MT
metaDescription: Broadus is the Powder River County seat, on the Cedar Creek Anticline's southern reach. A retired engineer explains the courthouse records and real value here.
heroLead: Broadus is the county seat for one of the emptiest counties in Montana, and its courthouse is the only place I'd trust for a real title answer on land in this part of the state.
intro: As Powder River County's seat, Broadus holds the recorded deed and lease history for a county that's ranching territory first, oil and gas territory a distant second. The Cedar Creek Anticline's southern reach passes through the county, and there's been scattered coalbed methane interest near the Wyoming line, but neither compares to the production intensity of Montana's more active basins.

sections.heading: What the Broadus Courthouse Actually Tells You
paragraphs: A title search here will show your recorded ownership, any historical or current lease, and whether your tract has ever seen a permit filed against it. For most owners in this county, that search turns up either a quiet, never-developed interest or a modest legacy royalty from an older conventional well along the Cedar Creek trend, and I'll tell you which one you're dealing with plainly.

sections.heading: Realistic Geology for This County
paragraphs: Powder River County sits at the southern edge of both the Cedar Creek Anticline and the Powder River Basin's coalbed methane belt, catching some activity from each but never as the core of either. Development here has always been more sporadic and operator-selective than in the busier counties farther north, which is a fair, honest way to frame value expectations rather than an optimistic one that won't hold up.

sections.heading: Building a Fair Offer
paragraphs: I look at whatever production or lease history the courthouse search turns up, weigh it against current activity levels in the county, and give a range that reflects Powder River County's genuinely quieter position rather than borrowing numbers from busier basins. If your interest has real production behind it, I'll build the offer off that data specifically.

faqs.question: Where is the courthouse for Powder River County mineral records?
faqs.answer: The Powder River County Clerk and Recorder's office is in Broadus, the county seat, and holds the recorded deeds and lease history for the entire county.

faqs.question: Is Powder River County an active oil and gas area?
faqs.answer: It's on the edge of both the Cedar Creek Anticline and the Powder River Basin's coalbed methane belt, but it's never been the core of either. Development here has historically been more sporadic than in busier Montana counties.

faqs.question: How do I know if my land near Broadus has ever been leased?
faqs.answer: A title search at the county courthouse will show any recorded lease history. If nothing appears, your interest has likely never been under active lease, which is common in this part of the state.
